alternatives.argument: The algorithm explicitly maps a proposal draw through f(x) tilde-p(x)/(Z_p q(x)) on q>0, uses the support condition on the nonzero target integrand, and returns the sample mean; it declares all domains and the zero-density convention.

For each draw, change variables under Q to obtain E_Q Y_i=Z_p^{-1} integral(f tilde-p)=pi f; finite-sum linearity gives the estimator expectation. The support and absolute-integrability hypotheses justify the ratio and finite integral.

The weighted outputs are IID by the algorithm and measurable-image independence. The BCS-25 mean-moments theorem yields the exact sample-mean variance under the finite weighted second moment; change of variables gives E_Q[Y_1^2]=Z_p^-2 integral_{q>0}(f^2 tilde-p^2/q). Under AC and positive variance, the BCS-25 scalar CLT gives the normal limit. At zero variance, the nonnegative-integral-zero theorem makes Y_1=theta almost surely, so each finite sample mean has the degenerate N(0,0) law.
For nonnegative unnormalized weights W_i=tilde-p(X_i)/q(X_i), the procedure returns the weighted ratio when the denominator is positive and a named no-estimate status otherwise.

Under q>0 pi-a.e. and the stated integrability, change of variables gives E_Q[W_i]=Z_p and E_Q[W_i f(X_i)]=Z_p theta. Measurable-image independence and the common proposal law make both transformed sequences IID. The BCS-25 mean-consistency theorem applies separately to the denominator and numerator averages; the positive denominator limit makes the ratio converge almost surely.

Apply the bivariate IID CLT to (W,Wf), differentiate t/s at (Z_p,Z_p pi f), and simplify its covariance to Z_p^-2 E_q[W^2(f-pi f)^2]. For the plug-in MCSE, use the choice-free SLLN on W^2, W^2(f-pi f), and W^2(f-pi f)^2, with Holder for the cross moment.

For finite nonnegative observed weights with positive sum, define (sum W_i)^2/sum W_i^2 as a weight-only imbalance diagnostic; the companion finite two-point counterexample shows it does not certify target support coverage.
